item.title: ‘We just watched Jeremiah Smith play his last snap at Ohio State’: Analyst says Jeremiah Smith is ‘done’ after Oregon loss
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) reacts during the NCAA football game against USC Trojans at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum on Oct. 31, 2026. The Ohio State Buckeyes’ season took another hit on Saturday with a 41-28 loss to Oregon, and star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith’s frustration was on full display. Now, one analyst thinks Smith may have already played his final game for the Buckeyes. Former NFL running back Damien Harris predicted after the game that Smith won’t play again this season, arguing that there’s nothing left for him to play for. But Harris also made one claim that doesn’t quite line up with reality, saying that Smith is “not going to get a Heisman” this year. Ohio State’s Tough Stretch Ohio State jumped out to a 14-0 lead over Oregon at Ohio Stadium, but the Ducks responded with 38 straight points. It was the Buckeyes’ second straight loss after a 30-18 defeat at USC, and head coach Ryan Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. Smith went more than two full quarters without a catch against Oregon, and he was seen yelling toward the Ohio State sideline late in the third quarter. One Ohio State reporter even called Smith “a petulant child” for his behavior. Smith’s usage had already been a hot topic after the USC loss, when Fox’s Joel Klatt said that Ohio State’s approach with its star receiver “can’t be your game plan.” Smith did eventually get going against Oregon, finishing with seven catches for 133 yards and a touchdown. The loss dropped Ohio State to 6-3, and with starting quarterback Julian Sayin sidelined by an arm injury, the Buckeyes’ College Football Playoff hopes are all but gone. ‘What’s there to play for?’ Speaking on CBS Sports’ postgame show, Harris said he believes that Smith is done for the season. “We just watched Jeremiah Smith play his last snap at Ohio State. He’s done. He’s gonna pack it up. He’s not playing anymore this season. The season is gone. We saw, this isn’t a College Football Playoff team. They were already on the outside looking in. The season’s over. He’s already etched his name in history. He’s got the touchdown record, he’s got the reception record, he’s got a national championship. He’s not going to get a Heisman this year. What’s there to play for?” Harris said, via CBS Sports . Harris acknowledged that the Buckeyes still have their rivalry game against Michigan left to play, but he didn’t think that would be enough to keep Smith on the field. “In my opinion, there’s nothing to gain, there’s everything to lose if you’re Jeremiah Smith. I don’t think that he plays again for the rest of the season for Ohio State,” Harris said. “There are bigger things out there for Jeremiah Smith than what the rest of this season has to offer.” However, Harris’ claim that Smith isn’t going to win the Heisman isn’t a sure thing. item.title: Wife of fan ejected from Lakers-Kings game breaks silence on Luka Doncic confrontation
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images One Sacramento Kings fan was ejected from the game against the LA Lakers after throwing a ball at a referee, after which he was confronted by Luka Doncic. Doncic asked the fan why he would throw the ball so aggressively at the referee, and the official instantly had him removed from the game. The fan tried to plead his innocence, as he suggested that he had no intention of trying to hurt or harm the referee with his actions. Sacramento Kings fan’s wife defends him after viral ejection Taking to Instagram , Kellie DeMarco, the wife of the fan who was ejected from the Sacramento Kings vs. LA Lakers game, addressed the incident. Rather than getting defensive, DeMarco took it in stride, joking that her husband’s past as a basketball player led to the hard pass, and he regrets how it came across. She wrote: “Yes, this is my sweet husband, and yes, he’s the guy who got ejected from an NBA game! I spent nearly 20 years in TV news, and he’s getting more airtime than me! He played basketball for years, and apparently the chest pass muscle memory never left him. “He meant no harm, he feels terrible that it came across the wrong way, and he has nothing but respect for the officials. Thank you for all the kind messages. We love the Kings and this community. And no, he is not Steve Kerr, I’ve read the comments.” When DeMarco’s husband made such an aggressive pass to the referee, Luka Doncic, who has a long history of issues with the referees himself, asked the fan why he did that. The incident quickly went viral, with many fans questioning why a fairly docile incident led to a fan ejection, given the precedent set for what it takes for a fan to be ejected. Hopefully, the Kings can reach out to the couple and offer them tickets for another game, given that the incident was nothing more than a misunderstanding. item.title: Walsh-inspired Australia crush irate Samoa to reach World Cup final
item.description: Reece Walsh (left) celebrated his first try with a spectacular backflip in Sydney [Getty Images] Australia (26) 44 Tries: Walsh 3, Dearden, Preston, Trbojevic, Best, Bostock Goals: Munster 6 Samoa (2) 12 Tries: Crichton, Tago Goal: Crichton Penalty: Crichton Before kick-off, Samoa's ceremonial war dance - the Siva Tau - turned into an intense face-off, with their players going right into the faces of their Australian opponents, and a couple even going forehead to forehead. It turned out to be the closest Samoa got to Australia all evening. Australia dominated at Sydney Football Stadium, triumphing 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final. In a repeat of the previous World Cup final, a worked-up Samoa side lost their way with errors and ill-discipline, allowing Australia to run in eight tries, including a Reece Walsh hat-trick. Australia - who have won the past three world titles in a row - will face New Zealand in Brisbane next Sunday with kick-off at 08:35 GMT. Walsh hat-trick helps Australia into RL World Cup final - as it happened Samoa had taken the lead after three minutes when Stephen Crichton – whose golden-point drop goal beat England in the 2022 semi-final – landed a penalty in front of the posts. But Australia led soon after when Tom Dearden picked up from a scrum and blasted through the non-existent line to score. Australia's next two tries came after they got six again thanks to poor Samoa discipline. Jacob Preston burst under the posts on 15 minutes; 10 minutes later, joint-top World Cup scorer Tom Trbojevic scored his eighth try of the tournament, benefiting after Crichton reached into the ruck. Walsh got in on the party - celebrating with a backflip - and the scoring was topped before half-time when Bradman Best bounced off tackles and into the corner. Both sides were fired up by regional rivalry, as the Siva Tau showed pre-match. Samoa's Brian To'o leaned his forehead into the face of Tino Fa'asuamaleaui, the Australia prop who played for Samoa in 2019. But Samoa's passion dissolved into frustration as the game got away - not helped by some questionable refereeing decisions. The most egregious came on the half-hour, when Crichton appeared to have grounded to close the score to 16-6 after Francis Manuleleua had beaten Walsh to a high ball. But a slow-motion replay led to the debatable conclusion Manuleleua had knocked on. It was the final straw for some Samoa players - Spencer Leniu was sin-binned for speaking out of turn to referee Adam Gee just before the break. Crichton did get his try in the second half after Walsh dropped a bomb, and Isack Tago scored in the corner with 18 minutes left But Walsh quickly responded after both Samoan scores, keeping them at arm's length while scoring his first international hat-trick. Bostock added gloss with eight to go. The damage was done - mostly by Samoa to themselves. Matt's player of the match: Jacob Preston I loved the industry and punch of Jacob Preston's work

item.title: Sinners & Saints: Roma 3, Sassuolo 0
item.description: Roma's Portugese midfielder #86 Rodrigo Mora celebrates after scoring a goal during the Italian Serie A football match between AS Roma and Sassuolo at the Olympic Stadium in Rome on November 7 2026. (Photo by Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images After Roma’s midweek embarrassment against Manchester United (which I’m sure my Red Devils friends will never let me hear the end of), the Giallorossi were in dire need of a strong statement win to right the ship and continue their hunt for serious glory in Serie A. Thankfully, a struggling Sassuolo side obliged them, and thanks to some saintly performances by several players, Roma ended the day with all three points, maintaining pressure on Lazio and Inter as both sides face challenging opponents in match day eleven. As always, a clean sheet means that there are no sinners in my book (what can I say, I’m a generous pastor in this Church of Totti). With that in mind, we definitely have some halos to hand out as well—this was a thumping, and Gasperini and his men certainly deserve praise even if Sassuolo are not the most intimidating opponent right now. The Saints Mario Hermoso At this point it’s no surprise when the Spanish international ends up as a saint. Beautiful Mario was excellent at both ends of the pitch, and his strong performance in all stages of play was rewarded by a truly strikeresque finish to open the scoring in the 27th minute. He made a truly emphatic finish—one that I’d expect to see from Paulo Dybala more than Hermoso—and it was that finish that gave Roma the breathing room they needed to take control of the match. Hermoso was also practically flawless defensively, as has become the norm. He read the game exceedingly well, contained Sassuolo’s attack even though that was largely unnecessary, and that hard work resulted in Sky Sport naming him Man of the Match. Even with Roma’s defense feeling like an embarrassment of riches, Hermoso has clearly put himself at the top of the pecking order of Gasperini’s center-backs. His performance against Sassuolo makes it exceedingly clear why. Donyell Malen No, he didn’t score today, but Malen’s excellence as the tip of the spear for Gasperini continued today thanks to his overall involvement in the Giallorossi attack. Bobby Marley had a hand in two of Roma’s three goals today, and was a constant headache for the Sassuolo defense. That’s the kind of performance you need from your world-class striker when he doesn’t find the net himself; it opens up opportunities for players like Matìas Soulé and Rodrigo Mora to shine, which only helps Malen himself find more chances to score further down the line. Most impressively, it was Malen’s pace and movement that repeatedly stretched Sassuolo’s backline, not just his usual strong positioning. item.title: Late release, upright seam, heavy ball: Decoding Mohammed Shami’s sorcery
item.description: Few bowlers possessed the ability to strip a batter of his technique, judgement, and ego like Mohammed Shami. The fast bowler from a nondescript village in Uttar Pradesh’s Sahaspur, which literally translates to the “land of courage”, bowled with a big heart, indefatigable spirit, and unmatched skill over 64 Tests. Former England captain Alastair Cook’s dismissal during the Visakhapatnam Test in 2016 was a case in point. Shami bowled a series of outswingers that forced Cook to play away from his body. On cue, he then delivered a perfect inswinger that jagged back sharply to sneak past Cook's defence and cannon onto the stumps. “It’s all in those beautiful wrists,” Shami’s childhood coach Badruddin Siddiqui told TOI. “The reason for his success was that he released the ball late and did not rush through his action. This helped him extract late swing off the track. With those malleable wrists, he made subtle changes at the point of release that batters found hard to pick,” the coach demystified Shami’s skill set. Like S Sreesanth, Shami possessed one of the most upright, God-gifted seam positions in world cricket. Shami was also a bit of a paradox because of the ability to make the old ball skid low while also hurling the ‘heavy ball’ that flew past the batter’s nose. The ‘heavy ball’ — the delivery that pitches shorter and reaches the batter quicker than expected, and hits the bat with extra force despite bowling from a relatively smooth, upright run-up — became Shami’s calling card on numerous overseas tours. The 2018 Johannesburg Test was a classic example: he dismantled South Africa, cruising at 124/1, for 177 to hand India a landmark 63-run win. Shami finished with figures of 5/28, unleashing his trademark ‘heavy ball’ on the spicy Wanderers pitch. At times, he could be erratic even when the conditions were loaded in his favour. But without any warning, he would return with a magical, match-altering spell against the run of play. This streak of unpredictability made Shami irresistible, and it was instrumental in India winning more matches abroad, especially under Virat Kohli’s captaincy. Shami was also a great senior, who passed on his art and tricks of the trade to youngsters. “I learnt a lot of things from him during my time in the IPL. Subtle things like bowling at the death and with the semi-new ball,” Uttar Pradesh pacer Ankit Rajput said. At 36, Shami had been performing admirably in this Ranji season, picking up 14 wickets in his last three games. Yet, the constant snubs and time away from international cricket had hurt him. “He was trying hard to make a comeback. But after a point, he realised he was not going to get another chance in Tests, which is why he chose to retire,” Badruddin explained. “He wants to play the ODI World Cup next year. item.title: Oliver Glasner hails ‘special’ night as Nottingham Forest stun Manchester City to climb out of relegation zone
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-CRYSTAL PALACE-NOTTINGHAM FOREST - AFP Oliver Glasner has expressed his immense pride following Nottingham Forest's stunning 3-1 victory over Manchester City on Saturday evening. The Reds head coach described the atmosphere at the City Ground as a major factor in securing their first home win of the Premier League season. A landmark victory at the City Ground The victory was sparked by an opening goal from Jair Cunha, followed by a clinical brace from Liam Delap, ensuring the three points remained at the City Ground . This result marks a turning point for the Reds, who had been searching for their first home win of the campaign until the visit of the reigning champions. The significance of the result extends beyond the prestige of beating Enzo Maresca's side, as the three points have propelled Forest to a total of nine for the season. More importantly, the win has moved Glasner's side out of the bottom three, providing a massive psychological boost for the squad as they look to establish themselves in the mid-table positions. The head coach was quick to acknowledge the importance of the result for the club's momentum. Reflecting on the achievement immediately after the final whistle, Glasner was full of praise for the collective effort shown by his players and the vocal home support. "It’s a very special night. Credit to the players for how passionate they played and for the spirit. I really loved the spirit in the team and in the City Ground and the togetherness," said the manager on the club's official website . Overcoming the Manchester City pressure Despite the comfortable final scoreline, Forest had to endure significant periods of pressure, particularly after City managed to find the back of the net. Glasner noted that the crowd played a pivotal role during these difficult segments of the match, sustaining the players when they were pinned back in their own defensive third. The resilience shown by the backline was a testament to the tactical discipline installed by the coaching staff. The manager highlighted how the energy from the stands translated into defensive stability, preventing the visitors from turning their territorial dominance into further goals during a tense second half under the lights at Trentside. "After the City goal we had moments where we suffered and in those moments the atmosphere was incredible. We had the full backing of our fans and this helped us to overcome a tough period," Glasner explained. Liam Delap the difference maker The standout individual performance came from Delap, whose two goals effectively killed off the contest. The striker showed great versatility by scoring with both feet, a feat that did not go unnoticed by his manager. item.title: 'Worrying for everyone else' - Ex-England midfielder warns rivals that Arsenal are winning without even playing well
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PRAGUE-ARSENAL - AFP Danny Murphy believes Arsenal's Premier League title rivals should be incredibly worried after Mikel Arteta's side opened up a six-point lead at the top of the table. The former midfielder feels the north London club are achieving phenomenal results despite not playing at their maximum level. Arsenal extend Premier League advantage Arsenal increased their lead at the top of the Premier League table with a hard-fought 1-0 victory at home to Hull on Saturday. Martin Odegaard continued his outstanding individual campaign by scoring the decisive goal to secure another crucial three points. Meanwhile, Manchester City suffered a stunning defeat away to Nottingham Forest at the City Ground. Liam Delap inspired the hosts to a surprise victory, handing City their third successive league defeat and allowing Arsenal to build a six-point advantage. High-flying Brighton are the only team to beat Arsenal this season . They will look to close the gap when they host Brentford at the Amex Stadium. Murphy issues warning to title rivals Following the weekend's dramatic results, Murphy claims that Arsenal's title challengers should be deeply concerned by the current standings. The former midfielder noted that Mikel Arteta's side are sitting comfortably at the summit despite not hitting top form for much of the season. "I think what’s worrying for everyone else is they’ve got this amount of wins, this amount of points, and they haven’t really played that well," Murphy explained while analysing the weekend action on Match of the Day . "Maybe in the Chelsea game they were outstanding but they’ve just got over the line other than that." Arsenal on course for historic title Arsenal have accumulated an incredibly impressive 27 points from their opening ten matches of the campaign. Murphy highlighted that teams holding this kind of statistical advantage at this stage usually go on to lift the Premier League trophy. "These numbers here, 27 points after ten games, that club normally wins the title," the former Liverpool and Tottenham midfielder added. Murphy also delivered an ominous prediction for the rest of the league, insisting that Arsenal are in a wonderful position. He added: "There’s more to come from this team, make no qualms about that." Massive fixtures on the horizon Arsenal will look to maintain their vicelike grip on first place when they return to domestic action after the international break. They face a demanding away trip to St James' Park to take on Newcastle in the Premier League. Following their clash with Newcastle, Arteta's men must quickly prepare for a tough European test. They will host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League just three days later. The Gunners then will welcome Manchester City to north London for a match that could heavily impact the title race.

item.title: Why Barcelona star has been omitted from Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp
item.description: Why Barcelona star has been omitted from Germany squad by Jurgen Klopp Earlier in the week, Germany’s new coach Jurgen Klopp announced his final squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches. In what will be the second international break of the season so far, Klopp decided to exclude Barcelona forward Karim Adeyemi. While Barcelona should be happy to have the German at their disposal during the break, it should be quite concerning for the club that the player is no longer being considered by Klopp. Why Adeyemi has fallen out of favour Adeyemi’s fall from grace has been concerning. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) As reported by Mundo Deportivo , there are multiple key reasons why Klopp has omitted Adeyemi from the Germany squad and most of them are linked with his fortunes at Barcelona. While the former Borussia Dortmund forward initially had a strong start to life at Barcelona, his form tapered off after the first international break. Since the break, Barça played seven games in total, and out of those 630 minutes, Adeyemi has played only 237 – 37% of the total. In the first eight matches, Adeyemi had scored three goals and provided three assists. In the seven matches after the break, he has scored only one goal, which came against Galatasaray in the Champions League. Important phase for Adeyemi Karim Adeyemi must bounce back to form. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) It appears Adeyemi, after a strong start to the season, is heading into the same direction he did during his time at Borussia Dortmund. The German has been great in providing dynamism for brief spells, but an overall consistency has always been missing, especially after the break. This has led to Hansi Flick himself use him less in crucial matches, with Anthony Gordon now the undisputed starter. The Englishman is expected to start in tonight’s key encounter against Atletico Madrid as well. This doesn’t bode well for Adeyemi, who joined Barcelona to take his game to the next level. The forward, therefore, must prove himself in the coming months if he is to remain a key player for Barcelona for the foreseeable future.

item.title: Deion Sanders contract buyout, salary at Colorado in 2026
item.description: The Colorado Buffaloes continue to rack up inexcusable losses against winnable opponents, despite having a coach paid like one of the best in college football. Those two things typically go on for a long time without any resolution. Will Colorado part ways with Deion Sanders? Who knows, but with each passing loss, most recently a 20-10 defeat to Arizona State in Tempe, the answer to that question gets clearer. Results matter, and over the past two seasons, and truthfully for the better part of his four-year tenure aside from 2024 as head coach, the results have been nowhere close to good enough for the amount of resources poured into the program. For a few weeks now, fans have been wondering what it would take for Colorado to move on from Sanders. Well, it would cost a pretty penny. Deion Sanders' contract details In March 2025, Sanders signed a five-year, $54 million contract extension with Colorado that runs through the 2029 season. His base salary this year is $10.8 million, the fourteenth-highest salary in college football. Needless to say, Colorado is nowhere near the fourteenth-best team in the country, and even if the extension was not just for the on-field product, but also for what Sanders brought to the university and city, those boosts have died down as well. Sanders would make $11 million in 2027, $11 million in 2028 and $12 million in 2029 if he saw out the remaining three years of his deal. Deion Sanders' buyout details Like most coaches, Sanders buyout changes depending on whether he leaves or is fired. Colorado could also work out a deal with Sanders to lower his buyout if both sides want to part ways, but that seems least likely, especially in season. If Sanders is fired before the end of 2026, his buyout would be $25.5 million. In 2027, that number would decrease to $17.25 million. Sanders would owe Colorado $10 million if he left for another job before December 31, 2026. Can Colorado afford Deion Sanders' buyout? The biggest question remains whether Colorado could afford the nearly $26 million buyout, and the short answer is yes. If you factor in that Sanders would be paid around $34 million over the next three seasons if he stays, the buyout ($25.5 million) would actually save the university under $8.5 million ($2.8 million per year). The buyout plus hiring a new head coach at $4-4.5 million per year would be about $37.5-39 million, or about $1.5 million more per year over three seasons. A very doable number if that is the direction CU chooses. If you hire a coach with an even lower annual salary, say a current Group of Six coach, the change could cost less than $1 million a year. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Taylor Swift has made no secret of her love for baking, and she has even shared her treats with Travis Kelce over the course of their relationship. But now that Kelce is in the middle of what could be his final NFL season, the newlyweds have reportedly made some changes in the kitchen. According to a new report, Swift has cut back on the sweets to help her husband stay in shape. The couple has also reportedly been hitting the gym together and sticking to a strict diet as Kelce tries to keep up with the demands of his 14th season with the Kansas City Chiefs. Kelce’s Final Run? Kelce decided to return to the Chiefs in March after plenty of speculation that he could retire, and many believe that this will be his last season. At 37, he has had to work harder than ever to stay on the field, and head coach Andy Reid has even suggested that the veteran may see a reduced workload . Swift, meanwhile, has been right there with him. The couple got married over the Fourth of July weekend, and Swift has been a regular presence in her suite at Arrowhead Stadium this season. Swift has reportedly fully supported Kelce through the long football season, despite how much of his time it demands. And it sounds like that support extends to their meals at home. Cutting Back on the Sweets According to an insider who spoke to the Daily Mail , Swift has been working out alongside Kelce and has adjusted her diet to fit his training. “They work out a ton together,” the insider said. “They love to lift weights and stay strong, and they stick to a lean diet. There is a lot of protein in their meals.” Swift is known for her love of baking, and she revealed on Kelce’s New Heights podcast in 2025 that the two had gotten into making sourdough bread. She also famously made homemade Pop-Tarts for the Chiefs’ offensive linemen back when she first started dating Travis. But according to the report, Swift has “eased off” on the sweets because Kelce “needs to be in the best shape of his life.” That doesn’t mean she has given up on baking completely. The insider claimed that she still makes Kelce’s “favorite” treat, French toast, from time to time. “When she is with Travis, she does everything to support him because he is working so hard on football,” the insider said. Travis is on the back end of his career and clearly does not have the same athleticism that he had in his prime. That means that he has to work a little harder to make sure he stays in shape, and it sounds like Taylor is committed to helping him do that. item.title: What Steph Curry went and said in the Warriors locker room right after beating Magic 126-119
item.description: Photo by Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images The Golden State Warriors were involved in a thriller against the Orlando Magic. Steve Kerr’s men dominated the first half, winning the first quarter by 12 and the second by four, thus going into the break with a 16-point lead. However, in the third quarter, the Magic outscored the Warriors by 17 points and took the lead. Steph Curry led the comeback in the fourth, and with the game tied at the buzzer, the two teams went to overtime. The Warriors won by seven points in the end, and although Curry was the star of the show, he was beyond impressed by his teammates. Steph Curry’s locker room message to Golden State Warriors teammates after beating Orlando Magic If you just look at the scores and Curry’s stat sheet, you would think that the 38-year-old led his side to victory once again. You wouldn’t be wrong to think that, but what was really interesting at the start of overtime was seeing Kerr leave both Curry and Draymond Green on the bench. That shocked everyone, but the players on the court for the first minute or so helped the Warriors to go up by four points. Curry and Green then came on to finish the job, but seeing the younger guys deliver at such a key moment of the game really impressed the 2022 NBA Finals MVP. After the game, Curry reportedly went to the locker room and heaped praise on his teammates for their performance against the Magic. “Steve Kerr says Steph Curry addressed the team in the locker room tonight to tell them how much he trusts this group and gave praise to the bench and depth,” Dalton Johnson reported live on X. In his press conference , Kerr said: “He spoke to the team after the game about the contributions of the bench, and he mentioned how much trust that he and the vets have in the young guys. “So, we’ve got a good thing going.” Curry is absolutely right to praise his teammates. Leaving him and Green out for the first minute could’ve easily backfired, but the fact that it didn’t shows the quality of the depth. That is one of the reasons why the Warriors have now won seven games in a row.

The 22-year-old wicketkeeper-batter from Jhunjhunu has this season endured a turbulent domestic campaign marked by bizarre selection calls. After an ankle injury saw Sumit Godara replace him in the first game, a fully fit Mukul was entirely omitted from Rajasthan’s second Ranji Trophy match. The shuffling peaked when he was named for the third match, only to be abruptly replaced by Vishal Harsh the next day and relegated to the Under-23 setup. True to form, the Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) finisher responded emphatically, smashing 112 off 129 balls against Mumbai in his first CK Nayudu Trophy game. He was then handed the U-23 captaincy after original skipper Himanshu Nehra was promoted to the senior squad, only for the selection dynamics to pivot again on Saturday with his own inclusion into Rajasthan’s T20 squad for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. After leading the U-23 side to an outright victory over Bihar on Friday, Mukul is now home for Diwali. In a candid chat with TOI, the youngster reflects on his whirlwind journey, tactical growth, and an off-season developmental stint in the UK, remaining focused on letting his bat do the talking.
